name: Get Slack alerts for negative Google Maps reviews

parameters.content:
## Slack alerts for negative Google Maps reviews

## Who's it for

Local businesses, agencies managing client locations, and anyone whose reputation lives on Google Maps reviews.

## How it works

Every morning the workflow looks up your business on Google Maps via API Direct (pay-as-you-go, from $0.002/request), pulls the newest reviews, and remembers which ones it has already seen — so each review is handled exactly once. New 1–3 star reviews are posted to Slack with the rating, the review text, whether the owner has already responded, and a direct link — so your team can reply while it still matters. No Google Business Profile API setup or place-ID hunting: it finds your listing from a plain-text search.

This template uses the [API Direct](https://apidirect.io) verified community node — available on n8n Cloud and self-hosted n8n (search “API Direct” in the nodes panel). No official API access, developer accounts, or OAuth apps needed.

## How to set up

1. Create an [API Direct](https://apidirect.io) account, copy your API key, and add it as a credential in the two API Direct nodes (new accounts include free credit).
2. Open **Edit your business settings** and replace the example with your business name and city, exactly as you'd search it on Google Maps.
3. Connect your Slack account and pick the channel to alert.
4. Activate the workflow (the seen-review memory only persists on active workflows).

## Requirements

- API Direct API key
- Slack workspace

## How to customize

- Alert on 1–2 stars only (or all reviews) by editing the filter.
- Monitor several locations by turning the Set node into a list and looping over it.
- Swap Slack for Gmail, Discord, or Telegram — the review fields flow straight through.

### 1. Find the business, get newest reviews
A plain-text search finds your Google Maps listing; the newest reviews are fetched for it.

### 2. New + negative only
Already-seen results are remembered between runs (n8n workflow static data), so daily runs only process new items. The memory starts working once the workflow is **activated** — manual test runs always process everything.

Only new 1-3★ reviews reach Slack — with a note when the owner has already replied.
